questions.question: In human biology, what collective term is used to describe the specialized sex cells, namely the sperm and egg cells?
In human sexual reproduction, what proportion of the offspring's genetic material is inherited from each parent?
options: All of the genetic material comes from the mother
All of the genetic material comes from the father
Exactly half of the genetic material comes from each parent
The proportion from each parent varies randomly between 10% and 90%

questions.question: Where in the female reproductive system does fertilisation typically occur when an egg and sperm meet?
How does the amount of genetic material in a single gamete compare to that in a completed zygote?
options: A gamete has double the genetic material of a zygote
A gamete has half the genetic material of a zygote
A gamete and a zygote have the exact same amount of genetic material
A gamete contains no genetic material compared to a zygote

questions.question: What is the correct developmental sequence starting from a fertilised egg (zygote)?
What is the approximate duration of the human gestation period from fertilisation to birth?
What is the primary function of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing foetus?
options: To deliver oxygen directly to the foetus's lungs
To protect the foetus from physical impacts and bumps
To digest waste products produced by the foetus
To transport nutrients from the mother's bloodstream

questions.question: Which specialised organ allows the mother to transfer nutrients to the foetus and remove its waste products?
Which of the following harmful substances is capable of crossing the placenta from the mother's bloodstream to the foetus?
options: Chemicals from cigarette smoke and alcohol
Harmful bacteria only, but no chemical drugs

questions.question: What is a potential short-term consequence of a foetus being exposed to harmful substances like alcohol or tobacco during pregnancy?
options: Sudden infant death syndrome later in childhood
Low birth weight or premature birth

questions.question: In the male reproductive system, where are sperm cells produced and stored?
Which statement correctly describes how egg cells are managed in the female reproductive system?
options: Females produce new eggs every day throughout their adult lives
Females are born with all their eggs in the ovaries, and typically one is released each month
Eggs are produced in the uterus and travel to the ovaries each month
Females only develop eggs once they reach the final stage of puberty

questions.question: What triggers the physical changes that occur in both male and female bodies during puberty?
options: The sudden intake of different nutrients
An increase in daily physical activity
A change in the body's core temperature

questions.question: How are physical features and characteristics passed down from parents to their offspring?
options: By sharing the same blood volume during growth
Through the transmission of genetic material (DNA) during reproduction
By physical contact and imitation after birth
Through hormones transferred in the amniotic fluid

questions.question: On average, how many days does a single complete human menstrual cycle last?
What occurs during the menstruation phase of the menstrual cycle?
options: The egg is fertilised in the fallopian tube
An egg is released from the ovary
The uterus lining breaks down and leaves the body
The uterus lining thickens to receive a fertilised egg
